hints: Focus on what actually burns in the engine and what just gets very hot alongside it.
Remember the catalytic converter deals with CO, NOx and unburnt hydrocarbons, but it actually makes $\text{CO}_2$ and it cannot oxidise one pollutant with another in the air.
Think about which two primary pollutants need sunlight to start the chain of reactions that makes brownish photochemical smog.
walkthrough:
**What burns and what forms NOx?**

Think side by side with the engine. The alkane fuel like $\text{C}_8\text{H}_{18}$ reacts only with oxygen, not with nitrogen.

Complete combustion:
$$2\text{C}_8\text{H}_{18} + 25\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 16\text{CO}_2 + 18\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Nitrogen from air reacts separately with oxygen at very high temperature to give $\text{NO}$ and $\text{NO}_2$.

**Check incomplete combustion and the catalyst**

In limited oxygen we get $\text{CO}$ and unburnt hydrocarbons, but $\text{CO}$ is a reducing agent, it does not oxidise $\text{SO}_2$ to $\text{SO}_3$.

The catalytic converter converts pollutants into harmless gases:
$$2\text{CO} + 2\text{NO} \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2 + \text{N}_2$$
So it removes $\text{CO}$, $\text{NO}_x$ and hydrocarbons, but $\text{CO}_2$ is a product it makes, not a gas it removes.

**Link to photochemical smog**

The real secondary pollution happens above the city in sunlight. Unburnt hydrocarbons and $\text{NO}_2$ absorb sunlight and react through free radicals to form ozone, PAN and other smog components.

This matches the correct description of photochemical smog formation.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{C}_8\text{H}_{18}$ (octane) is a petrol component and it reacts with oxygen only. Nitrogen does not react with the alkane, it reacts with oxygen at high temperature to form NOx as a separate side reaction.
options.B: Incorrect. Limited oxygen does give $\text{CO}$, but $\text{CO}$ is a reducing agent, not an oxidising agent. It cannot oxidise $\text{SO}_2$ to $\text{SO}_3$. $\text{SO}_2$ comes from sulfur impurities in fuel, not from $\text{CO}$ chemistry.
options.C: Incorrect. The catalytic converter removes $\text{CO}$, $\text{NO}$/$\text{NO}_2$ and unburnt hydrocarbons by redox reactions. $\text{CO}_2$ is not removed, it is actually produced as a harmless product of oxidising $\text{CO}$ and hydrocarbons.
options.D: Correct. Unburnt hydrocarbons and $\text{NO}_2$ are primary pollutants. In strong sunlight they undergo photochemical reactions involving free radicals to form secondary pollutants like ozone, which we see as photochemical smog.
